qa_pairs.question: How can an Alliance researcher start Abaqus in graphical mode using JupyterLab?
qa_pairs.answer: To start Abaqus in graphical mode via JupyterLab, first, initiate a JupyterHub desktop session using one of the provided JupyterHub links (e.g., FIR, NARVAL, or RORQUAL). Next, highlight an Abaqus module like `abaqus/2026` in the left-hand 'Available Module' section and click 'Load'. An 'Abaqus (VNC)' icon will appear on the desktop; clicking this icon will automatically launch Abaqus in a remote Jupyter desktop.

qa_pairs.question: What are the main characteristics and limitations of the SHARCNET Abaqus license available to Alliance researchers?
qa_pairs.answer: The SHARCNET Abaqus license is operational until January 17, 2027, offering a free shared pool with 3 CAE (GUI) tokens and 54 execute tokens for all researchers. Usage limits are set at 1 CAE token per user, 10 total tokens per user, and 15 tokens per group. This license, including any dedicated tokens purchased, is exclusively for use on SHARCNET hardware, such as the Nibi and Dusky clusters or the SHARCNET OnDemand system.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for an Alliance researcher to obtain access to the free SHARCNET Abaqus license?
qa_pairs.answer: To gain access to the free SHARCNET Abaqus license, an Alliance researcher must contact technical support. The email request needs to specify that it is for use on SHARCNET systems and must include a copy-pasted Academic License User Agreement statement with the researcher's full name and username filled in. This agreement process must be completed by every individual user, not just by a group once.
